A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gravitational wave forms are given by the sum of the Newtonian part and the post-Newton part which is the sum of the post-Newton term and the post-Minkowskian term.

the gravitational wave forms and the luminosity from the circular orbits of the test particles around the black holes are given by the Newtonian forms with the Newtonian mass $M$ replaced by the effective mass $M_{\rm eff}$, which is the sum of the black hole mass and the reduced mass of the test particle.
the gravitational wave form and the luminosity of the circular orbit can be expressed by a finite number of universal functions of $v$ alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the logarithmic corrections to the gravitational waveforms and luminosity are of order $M/r_0$ and not of order $v^8$.

the post-Newton expansion of the gravitational waveforms is not a perturbation expansion in the mass ratio of the two bodies, but is rather an expansion in the mass of one of the bodies relative to the total system.
the $\ln v$ term at the $v^6$, $v^8$, and higher orders are not negligible in the small mass ratio limit.
